id: # Interior architecture: one empty loft furnished, re-imagined, relit and walked through, with a material board and a 360° lobby. Every run becomes an example for students of this speciality, beside the card's showcase (tools/maintenance/seed_examples.cjs --speciality interior).

caption: The site before the project: an empty brick-and-concrete loft, made from words as a stand-in for a site photo. Every proposal in this speciality starts from this exact room.
prompt: Real estate photograph of an empty loft apartment before renovation: a large open room with a raw polished concrete floor, exposed red brick walls, a row of three tall black steel-framed factory windows on the left letting in soft afternoon daylight, white painted steel columns, exposed ventilation ducts under the ceiling, nothing on the walls and no furniture. Wide-angle shot from the doorway at eye level, straight vertical lines.

caption: The empty loft furnished as a Japandi living room: oak sofa, travertine table, jute rug, paper lamp, sideboard, olive trees. Compare it with the empty loft: the windows, the columns, the brick and the camera have not moved. It added a second armchair nobody asked for.
prompt: Furnish this loft as a warm Japandi living room, keeping the room, its windows, columns, brick walls, floor and the camera exactly the same: a low oak sofa with linen cushions facing the windows, a round travertine coffee table, a large jute rug, a tall paper floor lamp, a long oak sideboard against the brick wall with a few ceramics, two olive trees in clay pots near the windows and sheer linen curtains. Calm natural afternoon light.

caption: The same loft re-imagined as a coffee shop from its depth alone: a green terrazzo counter, bentwood chairs by the windows, amber pendants, plants hanging from the ducts. The room's volume, its columns and its row of windows are kept; only the programme changed. A quick way to test several uses of one space.
prompt: The same loft converted into a busy specialty coffee shop, seen from the doorway: a long counter of green terrazzo with a copper espresso machine along the brick wall, small round marble tables and bentwood chairs by the tall steel windows, pendant lights in amber glass, plants hanging from the ducts, customers working on laptops and a barista pouring milk. Warm afternoon light.

caption: A lighting study: the furnished room on a winter evening, blue dusk outside, the paper lamp and two table lamps lit, warm pools of light on the brick. Every piece of furniture is where it was.
prompt: Turn <Picture 1> into the same room on a winter evening: deep blue dusk outside the windows, the paper floor lamp and two small table lamps switched on, casting warm pools of light and soft shadows on the brick wall, the corners of the room dim. Keep every piece of furniture, its place and the camera exactly the same.

caption: A product shot of an armchair (bent ash plywood, rust bouclé), made to be placed into the room in the next example.
prompt: Studio product photograph of a lounge armchair: a curved shell of bent ash plywood with a deep seat upholstered in rust-orange bouclé wool, on four slim splayed solid ash legs, three-quarter front view, centred on a seamless light grey background, soft even studio light and a gentle shadow under the chair.

caption: The armchair from the product shot placed in the furnished room, matching its light and perspective. It was asked to replace the sofa; it replaced the small armchair on the left instead and kept the sofa. Check which object an edit took before you trust it.
prompt: Replace the sofa in the picture with the armchair from the reference image, placed in the same spot and facing the windows, matching the light, the scale and the perspective of the room.

caption: The furnished room seen from the side, from the one straight-on picture. The windows and the brick follow, but the furniture does not: a second sofa appeared and the pieces moved. For a room, another angle is a mood picture, not a check of the layout.

A material board described in words and drawn exactly: oak, green terrazzo, linen, rust bouclé, a brass profile, clay, olive leaves, a sage colour card, and the handwritten label 'LOFT 04 - JAPANDI' spelled right.
prompt: Overhead flat lay photograph of an interior designer's material board on a white desk: a square sample of pale oak flooring, a slab of green terrazzo, a folded swatch of natural linen, a swatch of rust-orange bouclé wool, a short brass profile, a rough handmade clay tile, a sprig of dried olive leaves, a colour card in sage green and a handwritten label reading 'LOFT 04 — JAPANDI' in black ink. Soft daylight from the left, gentle shadows, everything neatly arranged in a grid.

caption: The material board made four times wider and taller (4736×3584) for printing on a presentation panel. Zoom to 100% on the terrazzo chips and the bouclé loops.

Press View in 360° in a hotel lobby: the green marble desk, the armchairs, the spiral staircase and the fig trees are there, but the floor turned to grass and the ceiling opened onto the sky. This card is made for outdoor places; for an interior it gives a mood, not a room.
place_2: the centre of a calm boutique hotel lobby with a double-height ceiling: a reception desk of green marble, a wall of vertical oak slats, low velvet armchairs around a round wool rug, a sculptural spiral staircase in white plaster, tall arched windows onto a city street, large potted fig trees and warm brass pendant lights

caption: Before and after in five seconds, from the empty loft to the furnished one: the curtains fall, the rug appears, then the sofa, the lamp and the sideboard, and the room ends exactly on the furnished picture. With soft sounds and piano. A presentation clip made from two stills.
prompt: Use the provided start image as the first frame and the provided end image as the final frame anchor. A before-and-after transformation of the loft with the camera completely still. Starting from the empty concrete room, the furniture appears piece by piece like a time-lapse: the jute rug unrolls across the floor, the oak sofa and its cushions slide into place facing the windows, the coffee table, the floor lamp and the sideboard appear, the olive trees grow up in their pots and the linen curtains fall from the top of the windows. The afternoon light stays the same throughout. Soft sounds of furniture being set down and a calm piano melody.
